2_one_page_opportunity_summary:
# P-11 — Technology Transfer Opportunity

**Technology:** P-11 — S. aureus phage K immobilized on electrospun Ti-coated catheter surface
**Buyer:** Anti-infection catheter company (e.g., Cook Medical, Teleflex) or catheter OEM with infection-reduction pipeline
**Current Evidence:** T1 | NONE
**Recommended Transaction:** SPONSORED_VALIDATION (phage coating bench)
**Validation Cost:** $10-15K (6-12 months to T2)

## Problem
Infection = 8-12% of shunt failures, $40-80K per case. Antibiotic resistance emerging.

## Technology
P-11 — S. aureus phage K immobilized on electrospun Ti-coated catheter surface

## Strategic Value
Novel anti-infection mechanism (phage vs antibiotic)

## What Is Proven
- Computational model: yes
- External verification: no
- Physical validation: no

## What Is NOT Proven
- NO_FAILURES_TESTED_YET — all evidence is MODELLED. Buyer should treat all claims as untested hypotheses until decisive experiment is commissioned.

## Strongest Alternative
Antibiotic coatings (resistance emerging)

## Decisive Question
Phage stability on Ti in CSF. Biofilm prevention in realistic challenge.

## What We Are Asking You to Do
Request technical diligence. Commission additional computational verification OR the decisive experiment. Licensing is a subsequent route after technical maturity is established.
